title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Yoga and Pilates
audience: Yoga and Pilates teachers and studio operators who want repeat bookings, course renewals and referrals from students they have already taught.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the student has finished a course and confirmed it met their needs, and that the student can decline easily.
Write a next-block offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the point the student is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the student has finished a course or series and confirmed that the classes met what they wanted. That is usually at the final class, or when the last payment clears. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you would like, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and what the student said. Timing matters. In one Baylor Keller Center experiment, 1.32 per cent of customers left reviews with no reminder, against 2.16 per cent with a late reminder (Baylor Keller Center, 1 June 2024). That is one experiment, not a yoga study. The AMA says experience goods need more evaluation time than search goods (AMA, 10 January 2023), and a yoga course is an experience a student judges over several weeks. Do not write reviews for students or invent them, and do not screen out students who were unhappy. Asking only satisfied students is review gating, which Podium says Google treats as a violation (Podium, 2 May 2022). Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, including for changing or removing negative reviews (Google Help, no date shown). The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next block before the student leaves
instruction.body: At the final class, propose the next step with a date: the next six-week series, a block pack or a regular membership. Put the scope, the interval, the price, the pause rules and the expiry of any pack in writing, and confirm that the student agrees before you change their booking. Pack validity is part of the offer. ASMY's public list says its six-class pack is valid for one month, its twelve-class pack for two months and its twenty-class pack for three months (ASMY, 6 November 2026). Reformer Pilates needs the same clarity: UniActive excludes reformer classes from its memberships and asks for cancellation at least six hours before a class to receive a credit (UOW UniActive, undated). If the offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Check in at an interval that suits the service
instruction.body: For a course, a check-in around ninety days is a suggested starting point to test, not a benchmark. The check asks whether the student's goal still holds, what has changed and whether they want the next block. Keep it short, record the reply and close the loop. A check-in that only asks about the result may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any class or pack can be, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023). Every commercial email or text needs an unsubscribe option, and ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days (ACMA, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Re-contact around the student's own dates, not seasons
instruction.body: The research found no seasonal demand data for yoga or Pilates, so do not plan around a season you have not measured. Plan around dates you can see in your records: a membership renewal, a pack expiry, the end of a course, or a term you run. Send a short message before each one, with the slots you can deliver, written terms and an easy opt-out. Do not pressure anyone, and do not contact a student who has asked not to hear from you. Record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that student.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the student knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide the reward, such as a class credit when the referred person buys a paid pack, and write the payment condition down. That condition is normally that the referred person has completed a paid course or pack. Stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across a set of studies (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023). Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017, an older source). Check any cash or credit reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, and no quantified referral data for yoga or Pilates was found, so this lesson gives no referral rate.

procedure: After the student's final class is agreed, make one review or referral request, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-block offer with a date, scope, interval, price approach and pack expiry, and confirm it with the student.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the service, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message before each membership renewal or pack expiry, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred course or pack is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each term which requests, offers and timings produced repeat bookings.

workedExamples.situation: A yoga teacher finishes a beginner series with a group of students. One student says she will recommend the class to her friend, who has never done yoga. The teacher wants to offer the student a class credit if the friend joins a paid series.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the teacher do before the friend books, and what should she avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes down the credit, the condition that the friend completes a paid series, and when the credit applies, before any referral happens. She asks the student to pass on the friend's details, and she contacts the friend only if the friend agrees. She does not promise a credit she has not written down, and she checks the tax or contract effect with an adviser if she is unsure. She does not offer any class or workshop outside the scope of her registration and insurance.

equipmentAndPpe: Student record with the final class date and the review or referral request made
Next-block offer template with scope, interval, price approach and pack expiry
Calendar of renewal and pack-expiry dates taken from booking records
No PPE is needed for student follow-up; any class follows the venue's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the student has confirmed the course met their needs.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after the final class or payment, when the student has confirmed the course met their needs.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a student's name, photo or class images without consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a student who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a student's name, photo, review or class images needs the student's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a student's behalf or invent them. The OAIC says the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) covers organisations with an annual turnover above $3 million and some other organisations, so check whether it applies to your business (OAIC, published 13 May 2026).

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.
Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). ACMA has been enforcing this area, so check each message before sending.

Renewal and auto-renewal: Victoria's guidance on health and fitness centre agreements (January 2011, may be superseded) treats auto-renewal as unfair unless the student can opt out at sign-up. A law-firm summary dated 3 July 2026 says new unfair trading practice rules take effect on 1 July 2027. That date is unverified, so check the legislation before you rely on it.
Prepaid packs must follow your state's rules (see the SOL-03 lesson for this course). The NSW prepayment position is unverified.

A referral does not extend your registration or insurance. Accept only the work your registration and insurance cover. AUSactive's registration criteria are not treated here as a state licence. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after the course is finished or paid, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-block offer is written, has a date and pack expiry terms, and is confirmed by the student before the booking changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-block offers with the date, scope, interval, expiry and student confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the student has finished the course and confirmed it met their needs, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next block in writing, with a date and expiry terms, before the student leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the course starts, so the student feels committed
After the client has confirmed the result is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of their class. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only; not a yoga study.

AMA, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: experience goods need more evaluation time.
Google Help, 'Business Profile review links', https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: review links and the ban on rewards for reviews.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position it describes was not checked against Google's own policy.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives disclosed and not dependent on review content.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the reward in the invitation. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017. Older source; supports the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: promotional service reminders can be commercial.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04 per research. Supports: unsubscribe honoured within five working days; inferred consent is narrow.

OAIC, 'Australian Privacy Principles guidelines', https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles/australian-privacy-principles-guidelines/, published 13 May 2026. Supports: which organisations the Privacy Act covers.

McCullough, 'Unfair trading practices laws Australia 2027', https://mccullough.com.au/2026/07/03/unfair-trading-practices-laws-australia-2027/, 3 July 2026. Law-firm summary; effective date unverified.

Consumer Affairs Victoria, 'Preventing unfair terms in health and fitness centre membership agreements', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/library/publications/businesses/fair-trading/preventing-unfair-terms-in-health-and-fitness-centre-membership-agreements.pdf, January 2011 (DOT5504/10). Older; check currency.
UOW UniActive, 'Reformer Pilates', https://uniactive.uow.edu.au/reformer-pilates/, undated. Supports: reformer classes excluded from memberships; cancellation terms.
ASMY, 'Mermaid Beach timetable', https://asmy.org.au/mermaid-beach/timetable/, page last modified 6 November 2026. Vendor price list; supports the pack validity periods only.
Not verified: tax and contract effect of referral rewards; quantified referral data for yoga or Pilates; the Fitness Australia position; the NSW prepayment law.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.

officialReferences.title: Online reviews for product and services (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: Says incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says. Publisher: ACCC.

officialReferences.title: Australian Privacy Principles guidelines (OAIC)
officialReferences.covers: States that the Act covers organisations with an annual turnover above $3 million and some other organisations, without listing them. The full consent detail was not read; small business coverage is unconfirmed. Publisher: OAIC.
